technical_and_design_decisions: Adopt JUnit 5 as the standard testing framework for all acceptance tests, aligned with the project's Spring Framework 6.0 and Java 17+ requirements.

Use Testcontainers to provision ephemeral, isolated instances of external dependencies (SMTP server, SFTP server, Syslog server, mock HTTP server) for integration testing, eliminating reliance on fixed shared test infrastructure.
Structure acceptance tests to cover core happy paths and 3 common edge cases per module, prioritizing fast, reliable CI execution over exhaustive 100% code coverage.
Add all new test classes to each module's existing test source set, with no changes to the project's module structure or build configuration required.
Use Mockito to mock internal module dependencies where needed to isolate the module under test and reduce test flakiness.
Reuse any existing project test utilities (e.g., common assertion helpers, test data generators) where available to minimize duplicate work.
assumptions: All 8 target modules have stable, functional implementations with no critical blocking bugs that would prevent test development and execution.
The project's existing CI pipeline is pre-configured with Docker support (required for Testcontainers) and requires no modifications to execute the new integration test suites.
Public functional requirements and API documentation for all 8 modules are up-to-date and available, eliminating the need for extensive reverse-engineering of module behavior.
Required test dependencies (JUnit 5, Testcontainers, Mockito) are already approved and present in the project's dependency management system, so no new dependency approval processes are needed.

Sample test data (e.g., sample PMML models, sample SFTP files, sample Syslog messages, test email payloads) are either already available in the project's test resources or can be easily generated without additional tooling or infrastructure.
The developer has existing working knowledge of the functionality of all 8 target modules, so no additional ramp-up time for domain or module-specific knowledge is required.
Acceptance tests are only required to validate functional correctness and CI reliability, with no requirements for testing non-functional attributes such as performance, load, or security.
